newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli utlility to start talks on Egyptian gas.
newsitem.headline: Israeli utlility to start talks on Egyptian gas.

text.p: Israel Electric Corp is expected to begin talks in the next few weeks with Amoco Corp and Agip SpA to import Egyptian natural gas, an official at Israel's Infrastructure Ministry said on Monday.

The official confirmed reports that Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon had held discussions with officials at Amoco and Agip about a proposed natural gas pipeline from Egypt. Both companies are developing gas fields in the Nile delta.
The direct talks between Israel Electric and Amoco and Agip are aimed at circumventing direct negotiations between the Israeli and Egyptian governments, industry sources said.

Israel has been holding dicussions for the last few years in an effort to reach a long-term agreement on gas sales, but little progress has been made. The ministry source said Cairo had now agreed to let Amoco and Agip reach agreements directly with Israeli customers.
"Israel Electric would be the main customer for the natural gas and that is the reason why the talks are so important," the official said.
State-owned Israel Electric is the country's sole electrical utility.
The ministry is also considering a proposal to construct an undersea pipeline between Egypt and Israel that officials say would be more secure than the overland pipeline originally planned.
The undersea pipeline would run under the Mediterranean Sea where it would supply three Israeli power plants all located on the coast.
